markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (97%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class conformal set, clean input and second-model agreement all line up [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 97%, Normal 2%, InSitu 1% | Clearly separated |
| Conformal set | Benign only (α=0.1) | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.997 / 76th percentile | Typical input, no flag |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Benign [F5] | Mostly agree |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↓ invasive · Scarce here, which lowers the concept-model score · Validated [F2]
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 2, 8, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; linked to lower invasive likelihood · Unreliable [F3]
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 8, 9, 10) · ↓ invasive · Prominent, above typical · Validated [F4]
- **Neoplastic nuclei fraction** (regions 0, 3, 11) · context · 35% of nuclei, 72nd percentile of reference · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Deleting top 3 regions cuts the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Case leans on Unreliable normal lobules.

## Could be wrong if
- Cell segmentation covers only regions 0, 3, 11; neoplastic fraction (35%) sits above the reference median.
- Calibration error is 5% on a small test set (CI 3–18%); the 97% is approximate.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 3, 11** — Check whether nuclei labelled neoplastic (50 and 16) are truly atypical.
2. **Region 8** — Look for stromal infiltration; it is the strongest region for that concept.
3. **Regions 2, 8, 9** — Verify lobular architecture yourself; this concept failed its spot check (0/20).
